# FlipCanvas

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzPlus](BlitzPlus) · [Canvas](BlitzPlus-Canvas)

</div>


```blitzbasic
FlipCanvas:Void canvas:Int32, vwait:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `canvas` | In | Int32 | required | Handle of a canvas. |
| `vwait` | In | Int32 | `0` | 1 waits for the display to be ready, 0 shows it right away. Defaults to 1. |

## Description

Shows what was drawn to the buffer of a canvas, like `Flip` does for a window opened with `Graphics`. Until it is called the canvas keeps showing what it showed before, and `Flip` has nothing to do with canvases.

## Differences

* The window of the canvas is drawn and handed to the thread that shows it right away, so a program that never waits for events still shows its canvases. With `vwait` 1 the call returns once the window has shown the picture, at the pace of its display, and after a quarter of a second at the latest where the window cannot show anything (it is covered or minimized); with 0 it returns at once, and a canvas flipped faster than the display shows the newest picture. What was drawn stays in the buffer after the flip.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Flip", 20, 20, 240, 150, Desktop(), 3)
cv  = CreateCanvas(10, 10, 200, 100, win)
SetBuffer CanvasBuffer(cv)
Color 255, 0, 0
Rect 0, 0, 200, 100, 1
FlipCanvas cv, 0
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
